thread:
kai: Hey support — since yesterday our embeddings endpoint started intermittently returning dimension errors when we spike traffic. Most requests succeed but ~5% fail with "dimension mismatch: expected 1536 got 1024". We didn't change the client model, just increased batch size on our side.

maria: Hi @kai — sorry you're hitting this. Can you paste a minimal failing request and tell us which model you're calling and the exact client config (max_batch_size, dynamic batching on/off)? Also which region?

kai: Model is rwd-embed-1536-v2, region = us-west-2. Client config: max_batch_size=128, dynamic_batching=true (default), concurrency spikes to ~40 qps during the load. Failing payloads look identical to successful ones. Here's a sample error from our logs:

```
ERROR embedding-request: request_id=abcd1234 status=500 message="dimension mismatch: expected 1536 got 1024" model=rwd-embed-1536-v2 route=/v1/embeddings
stack: ValueError: embeddings shape mismatch
```

maria: Thanks. Two quick asks: (1) can you run a single-request curl that fails for you? (2) collect the response headers from the failing request (we want X-Redwood-Instance / X-Redwood-Model-Variant if present).

kai: Repro curl (most of the time it succeeds but if I run a short burst it reproduces):

```
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN' \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"model":"rwd-embed-1536-v2","input":["short text sample"]}'
```

maria: That's helpful. @aj from eng-runtime — this looks like it could be a coalescing bug in dynamic batching where different model variants or quantization paths get mixed into a single batch and the output buffer is sized for the wrong dim. We've seen similar noise on rare fallbacks. Any logs on X-Redwood-Model-Variant headers?

aj: Looking. Early theory: if a batch mixes requests routed to a lower-dim fallback (e.g., 1024-quantized shim) with 1536 requests and the runtime reuses a single output tensor buffer, we could surface a shape error when the per-request offsets are wrong. I need the failing request headers to confirm. Also need the server-side batch trace (we log batch_id -> variants seen).

kai: Attached headers from one failure (copied):
```
X-Redwood-Instance: rwd-rt-03
X-Redwood-Model-Variant: rwd-embed-1536-v2
X-Redwood-Batch-Id: b-9fc12
X-Redwood-Batch-Size: 64
```
No variant suggesting 1024, but the error says 1024.

maria: Odd. Can you run this short python script to do a controlled burst so we can capture a failing batch_id? It rapidly sends mixed small requests to trigger dynamic batching:

```
# repro_burst.py
import requests
from concurrent.futures import ThreadPoolExecutor
URL='https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings'
HEADERS={'Authorization':'Bearer '+os.environ['TOKEN'],'Content-Type':'application/json'}
PAYLOAD={"model":"rwd-embed-1536-v2","input":["x"]}

def call():
  r=requests.post(URL,json=PAYLOAD,headers=HEADERS)
  print(r.status_code, r.headers.get('X-Redwood-Batch-Id'), r.text[:200])

with ThreadPoolExecutor(80) as ex:
  for _ in range(600):
    ex.submit(call)
```

aj: If you can get a failing batch_id, forward it and we'll pull the runtime batch trace for that id. Meanwhile, short-term mitigation: set max_batch_size=32 or temporarily disable dynamic batching in your client so requests are sent immediately (this will raise cost/latency but avoid mixed-batch edgecases). Also try adding a small randomized jitter to request timing to avoid pathological coalescing.

kai: Setting max_batch_size=32 reduced errors in our quick test — went from ~5% down to ~0.2% under same load. We can keep that as a short-term fix.

deploy-bot: rolled config: runtime/patch-2026-03-14 applied to rwd-rt-03 (note: non-disruptive).

aj: We pulled the batch trace for b-9fc12 and see one anomaly: one of the worker processes reported a fallback request to an alternate quantized shard, but header didn't reflect this due to a race in variant-assignment. We're shipping a small fix to ensure per-request variant tag is attached earlier in the pipeline. Patch will be in staging for validation.

maria: Action items: (1) aj will verify fix in staging and schedule rollout to the affected pool (ETA 48h). (2) kai to keep max_batch_size at 32 for the next 24h and send any failing batch_ids. (3) support to keep monitoring and escalate if error rate not decreasing.

kai: Sounds good — I'll keep sending batch_ids. Thanks for the quick response. :raised_hands:

aj: For reference, workaround flags that helped during our test: set header `X-Redwood-Prefer-Uniform-Batch: true` or client config `prefer_uniform_batches=true` (server honors this to avoid mixing variants). We'll document this in the KB after rollout.

maria: Marking this thread as ongoing. I'll update when staging validation passes.
